claim: Every group with a faithful normalized-Hilbert-Schmidt unitary metric-ultraproduct embedding admits another faithful such embedding whose induced trace on group elements is the canonical group trace.
quantifiers: For every group G hyperlinear and every original faithful HS metric-ultraproduct embedding, there exists a re-embedding with trace 1 at the identity and 0 on every nonidentity element.
proof: Add a trivial block so a nonidentity normalized trace t becomes (1+t)/2, which has modulus strictly below 1 because faithfulness forces t != 1. The conjugation representation U -> U tensor conjugate(U) is a homomorphism with normalized trace |tr(U)|^2. After k iterations, the trace is |(1+t)/2|^(2^k), tending to zero. The outer ultraproduct over k preserves exact group multiplication and yields pairwise orthogonal group unitaries. Linear extension to C[G] is injective because the canonical trace gives ||sum c_g g||_2^2=sum |c_g|^2.

costs.dimension: From n_i, first use 2 n_i then repeated squaring: N_{i,k}=(2 n_i)^(2^k).
costs.efficiency: No useful finite dimension or runtime bound follows; this is an existence construction.

implication: C[G] embeds as a trace-preserving *-subalgebra in a finite tracial matrix ultraproduct and is stably finite. This complex-coefficient conclusion is already known for every group; the re-embedding is the relevant interface for the conditional stability theorem.

claim: Under the Cycle 3 common-kernel-word premise, if G is hyperlinear then there is a choice of hyperlinear microstates with word separation tending to sqrt(2), giving exactification distance at least sqrt(2)/L asymptotically.
quantifiers: Let P=<S|R> be finite and w a nonidentity word of expanded length L killed by every homomorphism of G to every sofic group. If G is hyperlinear, choose the canonical-trace re-embedding. Every exact finite-dimensional linear representation kills w, and the re-embedded unitary microstates have d_HS(w(A),I)->sqrt(2).
proof: Theorem 1 in Cycle 3 gives that every exact finite-dimensional linear representation kills w. Canonical-trace re-embedding gives tr(w(A_n))->0, hence d_HS(w(A_n),I)^2=2-2 Re tr(w(A_n))->2. Word telescoping bounds d_HS(w(A),w(B)) by L times the largest generator distance, so every exact same-dimension representation is at least d_HS(w(A),I)/L away.

costs.word: L is expanded word length; the candidate's 158-digit upper bound is not materialized as a literal word.

scope: This proves instability conditional on hyperlinearity; it does not exclude hyperlinearity or infer it from nonsoficity.

claim: The incidence-independent scalar array X_{i,u,v}=c_{u,v}I_D with c=[[4,5],[5,6]] over F_7 has maximal 2x2 rectangle rank defect but cannot be completed to the full local triangle wiring for r=s=t=2.
quantifiers: For every D>=1, over F_7 with r=2, s=t=2 and i=(alpha,beta) running over (Z/2)^2, no invertible choices of L_{u,j}, R_{v,k} satisfy all source triangle equations when X_{i,u,v}=c_{u,v}I_D and c=[[4,5],[5,6]].
proof: The cross ratio is 4*6/(5*5)=6=-1 in F_7, so rank(I-W)=D. The triangle equations and bijective shifted coordinates force L_{u,j}=L_u and R_{v,k}=R_v, then R_v=c_{u,v}L_u for all u,v. This forces every multiplicative 2x2 minor of c to vanish, but det(c)=24-25=-1=6 mod 7. Contradiction.

scope: This rules out only the incidence-independent scalar rectangle countermodel. Incidence-dependent full-wiring GL models and N65 linear-soficity remain UNKNOWN.

claim: The hyperlinear canonical-trace construction does not settle direct finiteness over F_p; no positive-characteristic coefficient or rank transfer is proved here.
basis: The trace-preserving embedding is over C and has no unital coefficient map from F_p. The exact HS-to-rank obstruction from Cycle 3 remains: U_n=e^(i/n)I has normalized HS error tending to zero but normalized rank defect 1. By Bartholdi-de Cornulier-Kochloukova Corollaries 1.8 and 3.16, the unresolved stable-finiteness gate can be tested over prime fields F_p, one prime at a time; no such general proof is obtained here.
